transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I guess the main thing is I’m just… exhausted. Not the normal kind where you have a good night’s sleep and feel better. It’s like sleep doesn’t really touch it. I’m a manager, so I’m used to long days and juggling people and emails and all that, but lately even getting through a regular workday feels heavier than it should.

And then I get home and dinner feels like this whole production, even if it’s something simple. I mean, last week I stared at a pot of pasta like it was some huge project, which is ridiculous, because I’ve made pasta a thousand times. So… yeah, that’s what brought me in. I’m just really tired in a way that doesn’t feel normal for me.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, even things you normally like doing?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I usually really love painting—like, I have all these brushes and paints set up, and I used to get kind of excited just mixing colors. And I love wandering through museum exhibits, even the weird small ones where half the labels are too tiny to read.

But lately my supplies just sit there untouched. I see them and think, “I should do that,” and then I just… don’t. And I’ve thought about going to a museum, but I can’t really make myself care enough to actually go. It feels strange, because that’s normally very much my thing.
Would you say that your mood has been consistently low or sad, beyond just not enjoying things as much?

Yeah… I think low is fair. Most days lately I wake up with this kind of heavy, gray feeling, like I’m already disappointed in the day before it even starts. Which sounds dramatic when I say it out loud.

It’s not always crying or anything obvious. It’s more like the tone of the whole day is just… muted. Like when the weather is overcast for a week and you stop expecting the sun, except it’s in my head. And then I’ll get distracted thinking, well maybe it’s work, or maybe it’s just getting older, or maybe I need to reorganize my mornings—but yeah, underneath all that, I’d say my mood has been pretty consistently low.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still, especially when you're not trying to be relaxed or energized?

I don’t know if I’d say restless… not really. More like slower, I guess. My staff has actually noticed it in meetings, which is embarrassing. Someone will ask me a question and there’s this pause before I can get my thoughts together and actually answer.

I used to be pretty quick in meetings—probably too quick sometimes, because I’d jump in before people finished their point. And now I’m sitting there thinking, okay, words, come on. It’s not like I don’t know the answer, it just takes a second longer for my brain and mouth to connect.
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or like you're not good enough, even about things you wouldn't normally dwell on?

Yeah… yes. I mean, I’ve always been the kind of person who replays conversations a little, like after a meeting I’ll think, “Was that too blunt?”—which, as a manager, maybe is just part of the job. But lately it’s gotten… stickier.

I keep going over every missed family plan, like if I said I’d do something with the kids or we were supposed to have dinner together and it didn’t happen, and it turns into this whole thing in my head about how I’m failing as a mother. And then any tense conversation with my husband, even small stuff, I’ll replay it for hours and think, “Why can’t I just be better at this?” Better wife, better mom, better manager.

It’s not even always something huge. It’s like my brain takes normal life things and turns them into evidence that I’m letting everyone down.
Have you noticed a loss of energy or fatigue that hasn’t improved, even when you know you’ve rested enough?

Yes. That’s actually a big part of why I’m here. I’m tired in this… weirdly stubborn way, where sleep doesn’t really seem to reset anything.

Like, I’ll think, okay, maybe I just need a quiet night, go to bed earlier, not scroll on my phone—though then I start thinking about that article I read about blue light and all the things you’re supposed to do before bed, and honestly it becomes its own chore. But even when I do rest, I still wake up feeling like I’m already behind.

Getting through a normal workday feels heavier than it should. And then coming home and doing dinner, just the usual stuff, feels like I’m pushing through mud. Not impossible, exactly, but way harder than it used to feel.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

A little, yeah. I’m not really… dieting or anything. I just find myself picking at meals more, or I’ll get through the workday and realize I never actually ate lunch. Which is ridiculous because I’m usually the one reminding everyone to block time for breaks, but then my calendar turns into this game of Tetris and lunch just disappears.

And I noticed some of my skirts are fitting looser lately. Not dramatically, but enough that I’ve thought, “Oh, that’s odd,” because I’m not trying to lose weight.
Have you noticed that your movements, like walking or even just fidgeting, have slowed down or become more restless without you trying to control them?

Yeah… not so much like I’m walking slowly, at least I haven’t noticed that exactly. But people at work have kind of noticed something.

In meetings, my staff will ask me a question, and there’s this pause before I answer. Like I can hear them, I understand them, but it takes a second for my thoughts to line up and then for the words to actually come out. Which is awkward, because I’m usually pretty quick in meetings—sometimes too quick, honestly. I’ve had to work on not jumping in too fast.

But lately there’s this little delay, and I can see people waiting. It’s not dramatic, but it’s there.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or not wanting to live anymore?

I… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had moments where I’m overwhelmed and I think, “I don’t want to deal with all of this,” but that’s not the same as wanting to hurt myself.

Sorry, I’m trying to answer clearly. It’s just, that question always makes me think about how people mean different things by it, you know? Like not wanting to answer emails versus not wanting to be here are obviously very different things. For me, I haven’t had thoughts of harming myself.
Would you say that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in most or all activities, even ones you used to enjoy a lot?

Yeah… I think so, unfortunately. I mean, not everything in a dramatic way, but the things that usually feel like “me” just don’t.

I usually love painting—like, I can spend a whole Saturday messing with colors and making a complete mess of the table. And I love museums, especially just wandering without a plan, reading the little plaques no one else reads. I used to joke that if I weren’t in management I’d just become one of those people who tells you not to stand too close to the paintings.

But lately my supplies are just sitting there. I’ll look at them and think, “I should do something,” and then I just… don’t. And I haven’t been able to make myself care enough to go to an exhibit, even when I know I’d normally be excited about it. It’s like the interest is there in theory, but I can’t actually feel it.
Have you had any previous episodes where you felt this same way—like you were consistently low, lost interest in things, and felt exhausted without relief?

Yeah… I’ve had stretches like this before. The longest one I can really remember clearly was maybe around five months.

It’s funny, I always try to measure time by work quarters or projects—like, “Was that before the budget review or after?”—which probably makes this more confusing than it needs to be. But yes, there was a period where most days I felt low and tired, and just not like myself. It wasn’t like one bad week and then it lifted. It kind of just stayed there for months.
How long have you been feeling this way during your current episode, and approximately how many times has this happened before?

This current one has been about a month, I think. It sort of started as this period where I felt really energized and driven—like I could finally get everything done—and then it dropped into this low feeling that’s been hanging around.

As for how many times before… I’m not sure I can give an exact number. I know it’s happened before, like we talked about, but I’d have to think through it more carefully. My sense is this recent swing has been going on about a month.
